Semantic SEO Writer - AI Agent Skill

71 research-backed rules for writing SEO-optimized, semantically rich content with AI agents

--- ## What Is This? This repository contains a **portable AI agent skill** that enforces 71 semantic SEO rules whenever an AI coding agent writes, edits, reviews, or optimizes web content. It also includes 3 companion prompts that structure the content generation workflow for blog posts, project pages, and data-driven SEO articles. Most AI agents produce generic text that lacks the semantic depth and structural precision modern search engines require. This skill solves that problem by packaging research-backed writing rules, grounded in Google patents, Named Entity Recognition (NER), and proven case studies, into a format any compatible AI agent can load and execute on demand. ### ✨ Key Feature: Ubersuggest MCP Integration This toolkit now includes native integration for **Ubersuggest via MCP (Model Context Protocol)**. By using the dedicated `ubersuggest-prompt-blog.md`, your AI agent can pull live SEO data (keyword volume, domain authority, backlink benchmarks, and SERP competitor analysis) directly into its context *before* generating content, ensuring every article is grounded in real-time search metrics. ### Who Is This For? - **Content creators** who use AI agents (Copilot, Claude, Cursor, Gemini) to write blog posts, articles, or landing pages - **SEO specialists** who want to enforce consistent semantic SEO rules across their content pipeline - **Developers** building AI-powered content workflows who need a structured set of optimization rules - **Agencies** managing content for multiple clients who need standardized quality controls --- ## The 71 Rules - Three Categories The rules are organized into 3 categories. Each category addresses a distinct layer of content quality that search engines evaluate during indexing and ranking. ### Category 1: Content Optimization (Rules 1–20) Enforces precision in sentence structure, citation format, featured snippet optimization, and content tone. | Rule | Name | What It Does | |------|------|--------------| | 1 | 40-Word Featured Snippet | Limits answers to 40 words to trigger featured snippets | | 2 | Answer Boolean Questions | Starts boolean answers with "Yes" or "No" before elaborating | | 3 | Answer Type/Listing Questions | Structures listing responses with clear formatting | | 4 | Author Rules | Avoids "if" at start, minimizes "also", statements before conditions | | 5 | Avoid Analogies | Replaces all comparisons with direct, factual statements | | 6 | Avoid Confusing Users & Bots | Restates info directly instead of "As stated before..." | | 7 | Avoid Coreference Errors | Ensures every pronoun clearly references a specific entity | | 8 | Avoid Everyday Language | Uses formal and professional diction only | | 9 | Avoid Linking to Citations | Mentions sources in text without outbound links | | 10 | No Product Promotion | Keeps informational content unbiased | | 11 | Semantic Triples | Structures info as Subject + Special Fact + Main Information | | 12 | Avoid Unnecessary Sentences | Combines related info to minimize token consumption | | 13 | Be Certain | Uses definite, factual statements instead of possibility language | | 14 | Be Specific | Uses exact counts and categories, not vague descriptors | | 15 | Verb Context | Matches verbs to semantic signals (increase/improve/develop) | | 16 | Cite Authoritative Sources | Cites sources before statements with "According to..." format | | 17 | Consistent Declarations | Maintains consistent stance across all webpages | | 18 | Consistent Style | Uses uniform tone across all documents and platforms | | 19 | Consistent Part of Speech | Uses same word role at start of every list item | | 20 | Content Length | As short as possible, as long as necessary | ### Category 2: Semantic SEO & Structure (Rules 21–45) Governs content architecture through context vectors, entity-attribute prioritization, discourse integration, and tense matching. | Rule | Name | What It Does | |------|------|--------------| | 21 | Boolean Questions Format | Reinforces "Yes/No" + supporting evidence with sources | | 22 | Context Vector | Creates logical flow from H1 to the last heading | | 23 | Cut the Fluff | Deletes all contextless words and filler | | 24 | Discourse Integration | Optimizes logical connections between sentences/sections | | 25 | Perspective Richness | Adds diverse perspectives after factual answers | | 26 | Entity Attributes | Includes relevant entities and attribute values for context | | 27 | Entities Over Keywords | Focuses on entity association, not keyword insertion | | 28 | Avoid Entity Stuffing | Prioritizes attributes by Prominence, Relatedness, Popularity | | 29 | Evidence Variations | Incorporates statistical, anecdotal, scientific, and expert evidence | | 30 | Factual Sentences | Uses objective, verifiable, clear, and direct statements | | 31 | Content Originality | Requires genuine expert writing, not rephrasing | | 32 | Semantic SEO Framework | Applies principles from 3,000+ Google patents research | | 33 | Examples After Plurals | Follows every plural noun with specific examples | | 34 | Subject-Predicate-Object | Structures sentences using semantic triples | | 35 | Content Types | Maintains Main, Supplementary, and Ads content balance | | 36 | Key Terms → Title & H1 | Connects key terms to title, H1, and topical map | | 37 | Long-Form Answer Format | Uses definitions, entity signifiers, and qualifiers | | 38 | No Context Breaking | Keeps related details within one paragraph | | 39 | Logical Information Graph | Uses simple transitions, builds on previous points | | 40 | Anchor Text Matching | Matches anchor text with target page's title | | 41 | Tense & Modality Matching | Matches tenses and modal verbs between Q&A | | 42 | Study Citations | Uses "A [Year] study at [Org] found that..." format | | 43 | Information Density | Maximizes info per webpage, section, paragraph, sentence | | 44 | Clarity & Precision | Uses Subject + Verb + Object/Modifier structures | | 45 | Subordinate Text | Matches first sentence under heading to heading format | ### Category 3: Advanced Techniques (Rules 46–71) Distinguishes expert-level content through truth ranges, unique n-grams, vocabulary richness, and perspective balance. | Rule | Name | What It Does | |------|------|--------------| | 46 | Parts of Speech | Ensures correct grammatical role for each word | | 47 | User Perspective Richness | Adds perspectives for different user types | | 48 | "If" Statements Second | States action first, then condition | | 49 | Prioritize Attributes | Matches answer attributes to interrogative signals | | 50 | Safe Answers | Provides comprehensive answers with multiple evidence types | | 51 | Remove Contextless Words | Eliminates filler like "basically", "essentially" | | 52 | Relevance Configuration | Restructures entity descriptions per query context | | 53 | N-Gram Consistency | Uses same key phrases at document start and end | | 54 | Ontology & Taxonomy | Connects entities through shared attributes and hierarchy | | 55 | Short-Form Questions | Prefers short question
